# Read-back

This is a backyard barbecue for about twelve people, built around a pork shoulder that will be smoked for approximately 9–10 hours total (3 hours to preheat and smoke unwrapped, 3–4 hours wrapped), then held in a cooler for 1–3 hours before pulling. While the shoulder dominates the smoker all day, the last two hours see parallel work: sausages and corn on a kettle grill (which must be lit an hour before service), baked beans simmering on a side burner, and coleslaw prepped and chilled. Two cooks are working; they have one offset smoker (occupied by the shoulder nearly the whole time), one kettle grill, one side burner, and a cooler for holding the wrapped shoulder. The text specifies no hard finish time, but implies service happens once "both cooks say it is ready"—after the pulled pork, grilled items, beans, and slaw are all on the table. The coleslaw must spend at least 45 minutes in the fridge before serving.
